hook: Instead of a monster, this file is about a young child with an unusual gift, and the containment section reads more like a care plan than a security protocol. Pay attention to the opening list of policies: library access, a mild peanut allergy, school lessons. The gentle tone is deliberate, and it makes the darker hints in the background land harder.
whyItMatters: It uses the esoteric Anomalous Human class together with a hazard rating, a format that frames the subject as a person first. The tags mark it as a rewrite. It belongs to the strand of Foundation writing that asks what humane containment of a child would look like, while still keeping the organisation's colder habits in view.
thingsToNotice: Notice the contrast between the care shown to the child and the routine instruction to dispose of every other modified creature once it has been studied. The recovery summary is full of redactions and project names that point to a much larger backstory without spelling it out. In the interview, the child's matter-of-fact answers about nurses, helmets and locked rooms say more than any report could. The few companions the child is allowed to keep are described with real affection, and they become the emotional centre of the file.
